summary_of_change:
Top-line revenue reached $234.1M in Q2 2026 (+62.0% YoY), translating to a current annualized run-rate of $936.4M. Growth is heavily driven by Space Systems, which surged 94% YoY to $189.5M, accounting for 81% of consolidated top-line revenue. Contracted backlog expanded to $2.36B, supported by major satellite bus production contracts and missile-tracking programs with the Space Development Agency (SDA) and the Department of War's Space Based Interceptor (SBI) program.

Capital allocation remains focused on Neutron R&D, Archimedes engine testing at Stennis, pad LC-3 construction at Wallops Island, and strategic roll-up acquisitions. Balance sheet liquidity stands at $2.13B ($2,115M net cash, or +$3.54/share) following $1.53B in ATM equity proceeds to fund operations and the pending Iridium Communications acquisition. Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow burn remains elevated due to growth CapEx and hardware assembly tooling.

market_pricing_in:
Rocket Lab trades at an enterprise value of ~$36.2B ($64.13/share) despite generating audited normalized Owner Earnings of -$0.34/share (-$201.9M total). Mr. Market is pricing in frictionless hyper-growth, assuming Rocket Lab will seamlessly evolve into a monopolistic, multi-billion-dollar space prime while ignoring persistent cash burn, dilution, and technical execution risks on its medium-lift rocket program.

Skeptics point to sequential launch revenue volatility—which fell 30% QoQ in Q2 2026 to $44.6M—alongside guided GAAP gross margin compression down to 29%–31% in Q3 2026 due to satellite bus component mix shifts and M&A integration friction. Technical setbacks, including first-stage composite tank structural testing failures, have pushed Neutron's pad delivery into late 2026. Relentless equity issuances, including $1.08B raised in 1H 2026 and $1.53B in ATM proceeds, have expanded diluted share count to fund acquisitions (Mynaric, Motiv, and the pending Iridium deal) and high R&D burn, leaving the current stock price severely disconnected from underlying cash fundamentals.
why_it_might_be_right:
The sell-side bear thesis posits that Rocket Lab's small-lift launch moat is vulnerable to SpaceX Falcon 9 Transporter rideshare pricing, while its Space Systems hardware business faces margin compression from fixed-price defense contracts.

1. Starting Baseline: Starting normalized Owner Earnings of -$0.34/share (-$201.9M total) and net balance sheet cash of +$3.54/share (+$2,115M total).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: Customer payload bottlenecks cap commercial Electron cadence, while aggressive SpaceX Starship/Falcon rideshare offerings exert severe pricing pressure on small-satellite launch ASPs. M&A integration overhead from Mynaric and Motiv compresses hardware gross margins, while fixed-price defense contracts (SDA Tranche) create severe cost overrun vulnerabilities.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Launch volume stagnates at 16 Electron flights per year at compressed ASPs of $7.0M ($112M launch revenue), while Space Systems backlog conversion slows to $600M annually, bringing total top-line revenue down to $712M.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Sticky fixed R&D expenses ($250M/yr for Neutron) and acquired operating overhead pull cash flows further into negative territory. Deducting cash operating expenses leaves degraded Skeptic Year-3 Owner Earnings of -$0.70/share (-$418.7M total), compressing Owner Cash Margin to -58.8%.

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: With negative owner earnings, business operations contribute zero capitalized earnings value. Sustained annual cash burn of -$320M over 3 years reduces liquid balance sheet cash from +$2,115M to +$1,155M (+$1.93/share across 598.2M shares). Adding a baseline asset liquidation value of $0.92/share yields a Downside Bear Floor Target of $2.85/share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
Modeling a disciplined 3-year extrapolation based on unit volume scaling across Launch Services and Space Systems provides a bottom-up view of Rocket Lab's normalized cash generation capability:

1. Starting Unit Baseline: Volume units consist of ~20-22 Electron/HASTE launches/year at ~$8.2M ASP ($178.4M launch run-rate) and Space Systems satellite components/buses ($758.0M run-rate), generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $936.4M. Starting normalized Owner Earnings stand at -$0.34/share (-$201.9M total).

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Year 1: Launch volume reaches 24 Electron/HASTE flights ($200M) plus scaling Space Systems deliveries ($950M) = $1,150M revenue. Year 2: 28 Electron flights ($235M), 2 maiden commercial/defense Neutron flights ($105M), and expanding Space Systems ($1,210M) = $1,550M revenue. Year 3: 30 Electron flights ($250M), 6 commercial Neutron flights at $50M ASP ($300M), and scaled Space Systems/constellation services ($1,500M) = $2,050M revenue.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization): Total Projected Year 3 Revenue = $2,050M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Deducting COGS ($1,271M at 38% gross margin), S&M/G&A ($240M), non-capitalized R&D ($280M), maintenance CapEx ($45M), and SBC ($60M) yields pre-tax operating earnings of $154.0M. Applying a 10% cash tax rate ($15.4M) yields Projected Year 3 Normalized Owner Earnings of $138.6M. Modeling 620.0M diluted shares, Year 3 Owner Earnings reach $0.22/share (Owner Cash Margin = 6.8%).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash of +$2,115M minus cumulative 3-year cash burn / FCF of -$200M (Year 1 FCF -$180M, Year 2 FCF -$100M, Year 3 FCF +$80M) minus cumulative buybacks of $0M equals Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $1,915M (+$3.09/share across 620.0M shares).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate g₃ exceeds 15% (turning positive from negative). Under the Narrow Moat matrix (Audited ROIC: -14.3% | Low Predictability), a 15.0x–18.0x P/OE multiple applies. Applying a 16.5x P/OE multiple to Year 3 OE of $0.22/share yields $3.63/share. Adding Ending Net Cash of $3.09/share results in an Expected Fair Value Target of $6.72/share. This represents an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of -52.8% per annum from today's $64.13 price.
